stem:
Krish sends several parallel light beams through three transparent objects in turn: a thin glass plate, a convex lens, and a concave lens.

Which claim correctly predicts what happens to the beams?

options.text: The thin glass plate lets the beams pass as they are; the convex lens converges them; the concave lens diverges them.
The thin glass plate converges the beams; the convex lens lets them pass unchanged; the concave lens also converges them.
These shapes matter only for a single beam, not when several parallel beams are used.
Any transparent object diverges parallel beams, whatever its shape.

teacher.key_rationale: Plate passes beams unchanged; convex converges; concave diverges. Swapping those roles, saying shape only matters for one beam, or claiming every transparent object diverges beams all miss that hinge.
